title: Isaiah Chapter 62 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 62 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 62 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 62.

questions.question: What will the Gentiles see according to Isaiah 62?
questions.explanation: The Gentiles shall see thy righteousness as stated in Isaiah 62:2.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:4, what will Jerusalem no longer be called?
questions.explanation: Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken as stated in Isaiah 62:4.

questions.question: What new name will Jerusalem be called according to Isaiah 62:4?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem shall be called Hephzibah as stated in Isaiah 62:4.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:5, how will God rejoice over Jerusalem?
options: As a bridegroom rejoices over the bride
questions.correctAnswer: As a bridegroom rejoices over the bride
questions.explanation: God will rejoice over Jerusalem as a bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride as stated in Isaiah 62:5.

questions.question: What does the LORD swear by in Isaiah 62:8?
questions.explanation: The LORD hath sworn by his right hand as stated in Isaiah 62:8.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 62:6 states that watchmen will hold their peace day and night.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:6 states that the watchmen shall never hold their peace day nor night.

questions.question: What will happen to the corn and wine of Jerusalem according to Isaiah 62:8?
options: It will be given to enemies
It will be given to the poor
It shall not be given to enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be given to enemies
questions.explanation: The LORD will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies as stated in Isaiah 62:8.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:10, what should be prepared for the people?
questions.explanation: Go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people as stated in Isaiah 62:10.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD delights in Jerusalem according to Isaiah 62:4.
questions.explanation: The LORD delighteth in thee, as stated in Isaiah 62:4.

questions.question: In Isaiah 62, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Prepare ye the way of the people
I will not hold my peace
Thou shalt be a crown of glory
questions.correctAnswer: I will not hold my peace
questions.explanation: The first instruction given is 'For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace' as stated in Isaiah 62:1.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 62:12, Jerusalem shall be called the forsaken city.
questions.explanation: Jerusalem shall not be called forsaken but shall be called Sought out, as stated in Isaiah 62:12.

questions.question: What shall the people be called as per Isaiah 62:12?
questions.explanation: They shall call them The holy people according to Isaiah 62:12.

questions.question: What does God promise about the land of Jerusalem in Isaiah 62:4?
questions.explanation: Thy land shall be married as stated in Isaiah 62:4.

questions.question: Who will eat the corn gathered in Jerusalem according to Isaiah 62:9?
questions.explanation: They that have gathered it shall eat it as stated in Isaiah 62:9.

questions.question: True or False: Jerusalem will be praised in the earth according to Isaiah 62:7.
questions.explanation: The verse states that Jerusalem shall be made a praise in the earth as indicated in Isaiah 62:7.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 62 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 62 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:5, how does God’s rejoicing over Jerusalem compare to human relationships?
options: Like a father rejoicing over his children
Like a bridegroom rejoicing over the bride
Like a shepherd rejoicing over his sheep
Like a king rejoicing over his kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Like a bridegroom rejoicing over the bride
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:5 directly compares God's joy over Jerusalem to the rejoicing of a bridegroom over his bride, emphasizing a deep, celebratory love. This metaphor highlights God's intimate and joyful relationship with His people, as also supported by the marriage imagery in verse 5 and the delight described in verse 4.

questions.question: What role do the watchmen play according to Isaiah 62:6?
options: They pray and proclaim the LORD continually
They lead the people in battle
They collect offerings for the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They pray and proclaim the LORD continually
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:6 describes watchmen on Jerusalem’s walls who never hold their peace day nor night, indicating persistent prayer and proclamation of the LORD. Their role is spiritual vigilance, which supports the establishment and praise of Jerusalem mentioned in verses 6 and 7.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:7 instruct believers to do in relation to God until Jerusalem is established as a praise in the earth?
options: Give Him no rest through persistent prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Give Him no rest through persistent prayer
questions.explanation: Verse 7 commands continual intercession—'give him no rest'—until God establishes Jerusalem as a praise in the earth. This ties to the watchmen’s unceasing vigilance in verse 6 and expresses the virtue of persistent prayer and trust in God's timing.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:8, what has the LORD sworn regarding the produce of Jerusalem?
options: It will be shared with all nations equally
It will no longer be given to enemies or strangers
It will be stored for times of famine
It will be offered as sacrifices to God
questions.correctAnswer: It will no longer be given to enemies or strangers
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:8 states that the LORD swears He will no more give Jerusalem’s corn to enemies nor allow strangers to drink its wine. This promise affirms God’s protection over the fruits of the people's labor, linking to the encouragement of faithfulness and trust seen in verses 6-8.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 62:9 describe the destiny of those who have labored to gather Jerusalem’s produce?
options: They shall sell it to foreign merchants
They shall eat it and praise the LORD
They shall offer it as a burnt offering
They shall store it for future generations
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat it and praise the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 9 emphasizes that those who gather the produce will enjoy it and praise the LORD, highlighting gratitude and integrity in enjoying God’s blessings. This corresponds with verse 8’s promise of protection and reflects the reward for faithful labor.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 62:6-7, what biblical virtue is demonstrated by the watchmen who 'never hold their peace' and 'give Him no rest'?
questions.explanation: The watchmen’s continual calling on God and refusal to give Him rest until Jerusalem is established (verses 6-7) illustrate the virtue of perseverance in prayer, showing steadfast faith and trust in God's promises.

questions.question: A believer is struggling with doubt about God’s protection over their efforts. According to Isaiah 62:8-9, what truth can encourage them?
options: God will punish those who work hard without faith
God has sworn to protect their labor from enemies and provide for them to enjoy it
Their work will be taken by strangers but God will reward them later
They must share their produce with all, including enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God has sworn to protect their labor from enemies and provide for them to enjoy it
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 assure believers that God has sworn to no longer allow enemies or strangers to consume what they have labored for, but that those who gather it will eat and praise the LORD. This provides encouragement to trust God’s protection and blessing over their work.

questions.question: What practical instruction does Isaiah 62:10 give that connects with preparing for God’s salvation mentioned in verse 11?
options: Prepare the way by clearing obstacles and lifting a standard
Gather the people for a festival
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare the way by clearing obstacles and lifting a standard
questions.explanation: Verse 10 instructs to prepare the way by going through the gates, casting up the highway, and lifting up a standard for the people. This preparation sets the stage for the salvation proclaimed in verse 11, symbolizing readiness and active faith.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 62:4 states that Jerusalem will continue to be called 'Forsaken' and 'Desolate'.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:4 clearly states that Jerusalem shall no more be called Forsaken or Desolate, but instead given new names signifying delight and marriage to God.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:3, what symbolic items does God place Jerusalem as in His hand?
options: A crown of glory and a royal diadem
questions.correctAnswer: A crown of glory and a royal diadem
questions.explanation: Verse 3 uses the imagery of a crown of glory and a royal diadem in the hand of the LORD to symbolize Jerusalem’s honored and precious status before God.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 62:2 describe the new identity Jerusalem will receive?
options: A name chosen by the people
A new name named by the mouth of the LORD
A name given by the kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: A new name named by the mouth of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states that all nations will see Jerusalem's righteousness and it will be called by a new name, which the LORD Himself names, signifying divine transformation and honor.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:1 reveal about God’s attitude towards the restoration of Zion and Jerusalem?
options: He will remain silent and wait patiently
He will not hold His peace nor rest until righteousness and salvation shine forth
He will delegate the task to the prophets
He will punish Jerusalem for its sins
questions.correctAnswer: He will not hold His peace nor rest until righteousness and salvation shine forth
questions.explanation: Verse 1 expresses God’s active commitment and zeal, stating He will not be silent or rest until Jerusalem’s righteousness and salvation are evident, emphasizing God's dedication to justice and redemption.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 62:11 declares that the LORD’s proclamation of salvation is intended only for the people of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says the LORD has proclaimed this 'unto the end of the world,' indicating a universal scope rather than being limited to Jerusalem alone.

questions.question: What are the people of Jerusalem called in Isaiah 62:12?
options: The chosen ones of the earth
The holy people, the redeemed of the LORD
The servants of the Most High
questions.correctAnswer: The holy people, the redeemed of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 12 names the people as 'The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD,' highlighting their sanctified and redeemed identity given by God, reinforcing themes of redemption and divine selection.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 62:7 teaches that believers should cease praying once Jerusalem is praised on earth.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:7 instructs believers to give God no rest until He establishes Jerusalem as a praise in the earth, implying persistent prayer until the goal is achieved, not cessation beforehand.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 62 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 62.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:9, who will eat the gathered corn and drink the wine?
options: Those who have gathered it and praise the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Those who have gathered it and praise the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:9 states that those who have gathered the corn shall eat it and praise the LORD, and those who have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of holiness, contrasting with the sons of the stranger who shall not drink it.

questions.question: In Isaiah 62:10, what is commanded to be done to prepare the way for the people?
options: Go through the gates, cast up the highway, gather out the stones
Build high walls and strong towers
questions.correctAnswer: Go through the gates, cast up the highway, gather out the stones
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:10 commands to go through the gates, prepare the way, cast up the highway, gather out the stones, and lift up a standard for the people, emphasizing preparation and clearing obstacles.

questions.question: Isaiah 62:11 declares that the LORD has proclaimed a message to the ends of the earth. What is the message?
options: Thy salvation cometh; his reward is with him, and his work before him
questions.correctAnswer: Thy salvation cometh; his reward is with him, and his work before him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:11 proclaims that salvation is coming and the reward and work are before the LORD, indicating a future redemptive act for Zion.

questions.question: What titles are given to the redeemed people and the city in Isaiah 62:12?
options: The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD; Sought out, A city not forsaken
The chosen nation, The favored city; Called blessed, The city of peace
The servants of God, The faithful city; The exalted, The city of light
The elect, The saints; The glorious, The city of God
questions.correctAnswer: The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD; Sought out, A city not forsaken
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:12 designates the people as holy and redeemed by the LORD and calls the city sought out and not forsaken, emphasizing restoration and divine favor.

questions.question: What literary device is most evident in Isaiah 62:4, where Jerusalem is given new names contrasting with former desolation?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:4 uses parallelism by contrasting 'Forsaken' with 'Hephzibah' and 'Desolate' with 'Beulah', showing renewed favor through balanced opposites, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God rejoicing over His people as a bridegroom rejoices over the bride, similar to Isaiah 62:5?
questions.explanation: Psalm 147:11 expresses that the LORD delights in those who fear Him and hope in His mercy, paralleling the joyful image of God as bridegroom rejoicing over the bride in Isaiah 62:5.

questions.question: In Isaiah 62:6-7, what role do the watchmen on Jerusalem's walls have?
options: They never hold their peace and give the LORD no rest until Jerusalem is established as a praise
They guard the gates against foreign enemies
They collect taxes from the people
They lead the people in sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: They never hold their peace and give the LORD no rest until Jerusalem is established as a praise
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 describe watchmen who continually pray and intercede for Jerusalem’s establishment as a praise on earth, reflecting unceasing vigilance in spiritual matters.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:8, what has the LORD sworn regarding the produce of the land?
options: He will no more give the corn to enemies nor the wine to strangers
He will increase the harvest tenfold
He will give the corn to the poor
He will destroy the enemies' crops
questions.correctAnswer: He will no more give the corn to enemies nor the wine to strangers
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:8 conveys God's solemn oath that the fruit of the land will no longer be food for enemies or strangers, emphasizing protection and blessing for His people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the proclamation of salvation coming to Zion as declared in Isaiah 62:11?
questions.explanation: Luke 2:11 announces the birth of the Savior, which fulfills the prophecy in Isaiah 62:11 about salvation coming to Zion with reward and work before Him.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name 'Hephzibah' given to Jerusalem in Isaiah 62:4?
options: It means 'My delight is in her,' indicating God's pleasure in Jerusalem
It means 'City of Desolation,' indicating judgment
It means 'Fortress of God,' indicating protection
It means 'House of Prayer,' indicating sanctity
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'My delight is in her,' indicating God's pleasure in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Hephzibah literally means 'My delight is in her,' signifying God's renewed love and favor toward Jerusalem as expressed in Isaiah 62:4.

questions.question: Isaiah 62:1 emphasizes God's refusal to hold His peace or rest. What is the intended outcome of this fervent proclamation?
options: Until righteousness and salvation arise for Jerusalem
Until the kings bow before Zion
questions.correctAnswer: Until righteousness and salvation arise for Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 1 stresses that God will not be silent until Jerusalem’s righteousness shines forth like brightness and salvation like a burning lamp, indicating divine commitment to restoration.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 62:3 describes Jerusalem as a royal diadem in the hand of God.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:3 explicitly calls Jerusalem a crown of glory and a royal diadem in the hand of the LORD, symbolic of honor and divine choice.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 62:12, the city will be called 'Forsaken' as a lasting name.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:12 states the city shall be called 'Sought out' and 'A city not forsaken,' reversing the former name of 'Forsaken,' indicating restoration.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word in Isaiah 62 is associated with the concept of 'redemption' or 'being sought out,' reflecting the status of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 'Ga'al' is the Hebrew root related to redemption, which connects to the concept of being 'Sought out' and 'Redeemed' in Isaiah 62:12, underscoring God's restorative act.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 62:2 foreshadow the universal recognition of Jerusalem's glory?
options: Gentiles and kings will see Jerusalem’s righteousness and glory
Only the Israelites will acknowledge the city
The city will remain hidden from the nations
The glory will only be seen after the end of the world
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles and kings will see Jerusalem’s righteousness and glory
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:2 predicts that Gentiles and all kings will witness Jerusalem's righteousness and glory, foreshadowing its universal recognition and honor.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 62 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 62 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:1 indicate about God's commitment to Zion and Jerusalem?
options: He will not hold His peace
questions.correctAnswer: He will not hold His peace
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:1 states, 'For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest...' This indicates God's unwavering commitment to Zion and Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:2, who shall see Zion's righteousness?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:2 states, 'And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness...' indicating that God's righteousness will be evident to all nations.

questions.question: What new name will Zion be called according to Isaiah 62:2?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:4 states that Zion shall be called 'Hephzibah,' symbolizing a transformation from forsakenness.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:3 say Zion will be in the hand of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:3 declares, 'Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD...' symbolizing honor and value.

questions.question: In Isaiah 62:5, how does God compare His relationship with Zion?
options: As a father to a child
As a bridegroom to a bride
As a king to his subjects
As a shepherd to his sheep
questions.correctAnswer: As a bridegroom to a bride
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:5 states, 'as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee,' illustrating a deep, joyous relationship.

questions.question: What role do the watchmen have according to Isaiah 62:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:6 mentions, 'which shall never hold their peace day nor night...' indicating their continual intercession and vigilance.

questions.question: What command is given in Isaiah 62:10 regarding the people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:10 instructs, 'Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people...' indicating preparation for God's coming.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 62:11, what is proclaimed to the daughter of Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:11 states, 'Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh...' emphasizing the promise of deliverance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:12 call the redeemed?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:12 declares, 'And they shall call them, The holy people...' highlighting their set-apart status before God.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:8 promise regarding the corn and wine?
options: They will be given to enemies
They will no longer be given to enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will no longer be given to enemies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:8 promises, 'Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies...' showing God's provision for His people.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Isaiah 62:7 regarding His commitment to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:7 emphasizes God's unwavering commitment as it states, 'give him no rest, till he establish...' showcasing His faithfulness.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:4 reveal about God's attitude toward Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:4 states, 'for the LORD delighteth in thee...' indicating God's pleasure and affection for His people.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5 and 11 convey about God's relationship with His people?
options: God rejoices over them and brings salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God rejoices over them and brings salvation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:5 and 11 together reveal that God not only rejoices over His people but also brings them salvation, emphasizing His love and redemptive purpose.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from the promise in Isaiah 62:9 about the fruit of labor?
options: It will be taken by strangers
It will be enjoyed by the laborers
questions.correctAnswer: It will be enjoyed by the laborers
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:9 states, 'But they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the LORD...' indicating that God's people will enjoy the fruits of their labor.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 62:3 teach about the identity of God's people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:3 states, 'Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD...' teaching that God's people are valued and honored by Him.
